newsitem.title: USA: Key Senate panel clears balanced budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Key Senate panel clears balanced budget amendment.

text.p: The Senate Judiciary Committee Thursday approved a historic change in the U.S. Constitution to require the federal government to balance its budget each year after 2002.

The fate of the balanced budget amendment in the full Senate is uncertain and the issue of protection for Social Security trust funds looms as a potential roadblock to final passage. Senate debate is to begin next week with a final vote by the end of February.

The constitutional balanced budget amendment narrowly failed in the Senate on two votes in the past two years, and Republican supporters say its outcome depends on the decisions of four freshmen Democrats who pledged their support during their 1995 campaigns.
The House passed the measure in 1995, but Republican election losses have made passage this time a close call.

If it clears Congress, it will have seven years to win ratification by 38 of 50 states before it can become law. The amendment is designed to make it tougher for Washington to run deficits or to approve tax increases to pay for higher spending. It also makes it more difficult for Congress to vote to borrow money to pay the government's bills.

Sen. Edward Kennedy's amendment to bar the use of mounting Social Security trust funds to reduce the size of the deficit failed on a tied 9-9 vote and he said it would be brought up again in the full Senate.
